events.period: By 2023-02-16; exact Ghana closure day undisclosed.
events.text: Jumia reported it had discontinued food delivery in the three countries. The operator attributed withdrawal to small scale and weak unit economics. This adjacent delivery failure tests rider-cost assumptions for commercial surplus-food routing.
events.evidence: Company financial-results exhibit filed with SEC; combined three-country metrics.

events.text: Samsung / M-KOPA accepted selected A-series phones as graded store credit. Promotion ended 30 December 2024. A real conditional price grid; no evidence the identical promotion survives.

Second-hand clothing imports rose from 230,535.3 tonnes in 2024 to 250,527.3 in 2025. Import unit value moved from KSh120,640.7 to 120,800.4 per tonne. Supply volume grew around 8.7% while price per imported tonne changed little. Domestic retail price and demand cannot be inferred.
events.evidence: National statistical office and revenue authority; tables 6.6, 6.8 and 6.10.

events.text: Basel amendments expanded prior informed consent to transboundary e-waste movements for bound parties. Test and document functional used stock and determine national classifications before shipment.

Fire destroyed a large area of Kantamanto; The Or Foundation committed USD1m in immediate relief. Capital, inventory, market access and the survival of uninsured stalls changed overnight. Recovery interviews a year later found uneven return to trade.
events.evidence: Local relief organisation; distinguish pledged and disbursed amounts.

events.text: Environmental Protection Act 1124 consolidated e-waste rules and replaced Act 917. A device importer must distinguish tested goods for direct reuse from waste; check permits, levies and take-back obligations.

Government decree 2025-181 suspended exports of used lead accumulators and their scrap for ten years from entry into force. Customs circulated instructions on 7 May. A dealer handling returned lead batteries must arrange a permitted domestic route. This is a specific chemistry, not all e-waste.

Refreshi and sector partners reported that 50 independently owned SPAR-format stores sold more than 23,200 surprise bags over the period. A better adoption measure than sign-ups; request store-day denominators and repeat buyers. Network merchant payouts and company revenue differ.
events.evidence: Reported study/partner figures; unaudited, original microdata unavailable.

events.text: President signed repeal of the E-levy. The statutory levy on electronic transfers ceased; provider fees and cash-out costs still require verification.
KOBA says it formed after the fire to unite section leaders. Coordinated access to retailers, tailors and cobblers became easier; it also concentrates gatekeeping.

Environment and Land Court set aside its July interim orders on implementation of the 2024 EPR regulations. NEMA later posted a 2026 FAQ. Read the current regulator instructions before costing a take-back model. A regulatory fee and a consumer deposit are distinct.

Two market leaders described reopening with continued capital and demand constraints; committee paid for security. Rebuilt premises do not identify liquid merchants or restored throughput. Include people who have not returned.

events.publication: 2026-02-06 customer reporting; PwC case page undated.
events.text: Customers received closure texts on 31 January. Kenyan KOKO group entities entered insolvency proceedings on 1 February. PwC explains that its carbon-credit sales subsidised the wider operations. Customers lost access to fuel tied to proprietary stoves. Verify the transaction without subsidies and plan an alternative refill route.
events.evidence: Joint administrators; consumer and outlet interviews.

events.text: Authorities cleared a section of the Gikomba shoe market on the night of 30 March for a river buffer. Merchants described immediate income disruption. Recruit displaced sellers as well as traders in place. A permanent stall address can disappear. Phase-one construction launch reported 14 April; individual relocations unverified.
events.evidence: On-site reporter, named sellers and zone chair.

events.text: AMA reported deploying collectors for a GHS2 daily toll. Small fees and sanitation payments affect daily cash position; request receipts separately from annual permits.
Annual GHS100 operating permit per shop took effect under KOBA–AMA agreement. Use this specific local fee in shop economics; it differs from AMA's daily toll.

Unearthed and Greenpeace Africa documented labelled UK store returns at an Accra scrap site and in shops, including some marked as faulty. Triaging a returned appliance and documenting final destination matter to workers and compliance; no representative failure rate.
events.evidence: Photographs, document review and interviews; chain inferred for some items.

events.text: Final PADCI e-waste plan mapped CIAPOL-registered downstream actors and distinguished local metal markets from exported boards. Seek documentation from actual receiving firms; a phone handed to a collector may become a component or scrap rather than a working unit.
events.evidence: Government project fieldwork and implementation plan.

events.text: Worker-led study interviewed 20 specialist Gikomba collectors after a multi-county survey. It documented who bears low-value sorting costs and why waste shares conflict. Track each batch from unsold inventory to reuse, rags and disposal. Unpaid or underpaid sorting makes apparent merchant margins misleading.
events.evidence: International Alliance of Waste Pickers; nonrepresentative original sample.

events.text: Four international brands and The Or Foundation unveiled the Apparel Recovery Coalition, with Circle Economy as secretariat. A 2026–27 voluntary funding route for demonstration work; enrolment and paid work for an unaffiliated startup were not announced.
events.evidence: Facilitator release plus Ghana News Agency interviews.

events.text: NCC identifies 7 October as the reference date for recognition of already connected phones. Its Device Checker FAQ tells second-hand buyers to verify status before paying. Put the national check before payment; it tests a different risk from hidden component faults or a seller’s ownership.
events.evidence: NCC FAQ and separate technical press report.

events.text: Yaga published its current fee guide: seller listing/selling is free, buyer protection typically about 5% of order value plus a fixed amount, with exact fee at checkout. Recalculate delivered-price economics at checkout; the updated schedule gives no universal fixed rand amount.

Tema Metropolitan Assembly opened a national competitive tender for waste collection skips. Read the attached notice too: ID /0022 and 10 Dec conflict with portal /0017 and 14 Dec. No bid decision without written clarification.
Kumasi warranty customer paid GHS 35 per bus leg for a nominally free repair. Cost to redeem a remedy can be substantial relative to handset price.
Buyer paid GHS 90 for jeans plus GHS 15 for alteration. A market delivers fit as well as access to stock.

Observed 193-piece bale cost GHS 2,200. Table projects GHS 1,522–1,609 if all priced pieces sell. GHS 591–678 potential shortfall before expenses; arithmetic conflicts with GHS 1,502 low figure in prose.

events.publication: WITS annual tables; release day unspecified.
events.text: HS 630900 reported imports USD 92.88m, 98.35m and 115.28m. National formal flows, not retail GMV or addressable fees.
Multi-site qualitative work and 60 interviews trace repair, resale and material recovery. Test speed-to-cash and worker compensation before proposing take-back.

events.period: Study period not exposed in abstract.
events.text: 621 shops and 279 SHC bales; 23.8% classified as textile waste by bale weight. Keep weight, later sales and final disposal separate.
27.1m active mobile-money accounts in October. Multiple accounts and merchant acceptance preclude a customer estimate.
376 traders; existing outlets included eateries and livestock farms. No kg of loss measured. Count only safe edible stock still available after existing users.
PEDL exploratory study uses structured audits to investigate quality uncertainty. Contact researchers, avoid duplicating audits. Final findings not yet available.
